### Observed differences

- In the later window, A14 disappears entirely (0 of 200 traces vs 91 of 200 before, about 45.5%) and A15 nearly disappears (1 of 200 vs 109 of 200 before, about 54.5%). [OCC001, OCC002, POS001, POS002, REL001]
- A21’s outgoing transitions were previously split among A14 (about 24.5%), A22 (48%) and A15 (27.5%); in the later window they go only to A22. A22’s outgoing transitions were previously to A23 (52%), A15 (27%) and A14 (21%); in the later window they go almost only to A23 (99.5%). [DIR003, DIR004]
- Relations between A14/A15 and A21/A22/A23 change from co-occurrence with ordered relations to A14/A15 being absent, so A21, A22 and A23 appear alone. [REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007]
- The lag between A21 and A23 shortens from 3 steps to 2 steps, and the lag between A22 and A23 becomes almost always 1 step instead of a mix of 1 and 2 steps. [LAG003, LAG004, LAG005]
- A14 and A15 no longer have observed outgoing transitions in the later window; the only A15 occurrence has A23 as its successor. [DIR001, DIR002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the later process no longer executes A14 and A15 as intermediate steps, so cases now go from A21 to A22 to A23 instead of passing through A14 or A15. This is supported by the near-total disappearance of A14 and A15, the routing of A21 and A22 almost exclusively toward A22 and A23, and the shortening of the A21–A23 lag from 3 to 2 steps. [OCC001, OCC002, DIR003, DIR004, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005] The number of qualifying evidence items is far above the 0.37 expected by chance under no change. [OCC001, OCC002, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, POS001, POS002, POS003, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005] A competing explanation is that the later window simply contains a different variant mix, but the size and consistency of the disappearance make that unlikely; the evidence cannot prove a permanent process modification. [OCC001, OCC002, DIR003, DIR004]
